sections.history: Vilamal, whose Tevaram name is Tiruvilamar, lies on the banks of the Odampokki river very close to Tiruvarur (sources give 1–3 km) in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The sacred tank is the Agni Teertham, and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Pathanjali Manoharar in the sanctum, with the goddess Madhurabhashini — also Thenmozhi Ammai, and in another reckoning Yazhinum Menmozhiyaal, 'she whose words are softer than the lute' — in her own, south-facing shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The Agni Teertham lies within the temple's sacred geography.
sections.legends: The lord's name Pathanjali Manoharar — 'he who captivated Patanjali' — joins the shrine to the great sage Patanjali, author of the Yoga Sutras, who in Shaiva tradition witnessed Shiva's cosmic dance and is counted among his devotees. Here the lord is remembered as the one whose grace charmed the heart of the yogi. The goddess's names, all turning on the sweetness of her speech, give the shrine its gentle devotional note; the fuller sthala purana is preserved in the local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a shrine near Tiruvarur. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail around Tiruvarur include Vilamal among their stops.
sections.experience: At Vilamal the pilgrim finds a quiet shrine by the Odampokki, close to great Tiruvarur, loved for its tie to the sage Patanjali. Before Pathanjali Manoharar and the sweet-spoken Madhurabhashini, the visitor touches the memory of yoga's great sage in a small Tevaram temple of the delta.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Vilamal is 1–3 km from Tiruvarur town, on the banks of the Odampokki river, in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur has its own railway station and bus stand, with local autos and buses reaching the village.
